days.title: Old City classics: bazaars, kebab and baklava

activities.title: Coffee and simit in Sirkeci
activities.description: Ease in with Turkish coffee and a tray of syrupy pastries at Hafız Mustafa 1864, a century-old sweetshop near the station. Order a half portion of künefe to share.

activities.title: Spice Bazaar grazing
activities.description: Wander the Mısır Çarşısı for pistachio Turkish delight, dried mulberries and Maraş ice cream. Prices drop noticeably on the side streets outside the main hall.

activities.title: Cağ kebabı lunch
activities.description: Şehzade Cağ Kebabı serves one thing: horizontally-stacked Erzurum-style lamb kebab carved onto skewers. Order by the skewer and add a glass of ayran.

activities.title: Hagia Sophia and Sultanahmet stroll
activities.description: Walk off lunch between Hagia Sophia and the Blue Mosque. Go late afternoon when the tour-group crowds thin; dress modestly for mosque entry.

activities.title: Boza at Vefa Bozacısı
activities.description: A fermented millet drink served with cinnamon and roasted chickpeas in an 1876 tiled shop — one of the city's most distinctive tastes.

activities.title: Dinner at Pandeli
activities.description: Turquoise-tiled Ottoman dining room above the Spice Bazaar gate; the sea bass in paper and eggplant böreği are the classics. Book ahead.

days.title: Slow morning in Cihangir, then the Bosphorus

activities.title: Long Anatolian breakfast in Cihangir
activities.description: Take your time over a Van-style spread of herbed otlu peynir, honeyed kaymak, menemen and bottomless tea. No rush — nothing else is booked until midday.

activities.title: Baklava stop on the way down to the water
activities.description: A gentle downhill walk from Cihangir to Karaköy for fıstıklı baklava and şöbiyet at the counter. Grab a box for the boat.

activities.title: Bosphorus cruise up to Anadolu Kavağı
activities.description: Take the Şehir Hatları public Bosphorus ferry past Dolmabahçe, the Rumeli Fortress and the wooden yalı mansions. Sit on the upper deck with tea; the short round-trip runs about two hours, the long one takes most of the afternoon.

activities.title: Kumpir and waterfront wander in Ortaköy
activities.description: Stuffed baked potatoes and waffles by the little mosque under the bridge — a easy, low-effort snack with the best bridge view in the city.

activities.title: Relaxed dinner at Karaköy Lokantası
activities.description: Handsome tiled dining room doing refined versions of Turkish home cooking and mezes — calmer and earlier-finishing than a meyhane night. Reserve for around 20:00.

days.title: Asian side: Kadıköy market and Moda

activities.title: Ferry to Kadıköy
activities.description: Take the public ferry from Eminönü or Karaköy — 20 minutes across the Bosphorus for the price of a transit fare, with tea and seagulls on deck.

activities.title: Kadıköy market crawl
activities.description: Fish stalls, pickle shops (try a glass of turşu suyu), cheese mongers and roasted nuts along Güneşlibahçe Sokak. Stop at Fazıl Bey for a properly made Turkish coffee.

activities.title: Lunch at Çiya Sofrası
activities.description: Musa Dağdeviren's legendary kitchen of near-forgotten Anatolian regional dishes — pick from the steam trays and kebabs, they change daily. Pay by weight; it's excellent value.

activities.title: Kup griye at Baylan Pastanesi
activities.description: A 1961 patisserie institution; order the kup griye — caramel, croquant and ice cream — in the little back garden.

activities.title: Sunset walk along Moda seafront
activities.description: Flat, breezy promenade with tea gardens looking back at the Old City skyline — the best free view in Istanbul at golden hour.

activities.title: Farewell fish dinner at Çiya Kebap or a Moda meyhane
activities.description: Round off with grilled fish and mezes near the market, then catch the last ferries back (they run until around midnight).

tips: Get an İstanbulkart at any ferry or metro station and load it for both of you — it covers ferries, trams and buses.
Book Pandeli, Asmalı Cavit and Mikla a few days ahead; the small meyhanes fill up fast on weekends.
Çiya Sofrası and market stalls are cash-friendly; carry some lira even though cards are widely accepted.
April evenings drop to around 6°C with Bosphorus wind — bring a warm layer for the ferry deck and rooftop bar.
Eat lightly at breakfast on Day 1 and 3; lunches here are the main event.
title: Istanbul for Eaters: 3 Days Across Two Continents
summary: A three-day food crawl through Istanbul for two: Ottoman classics and spice-market snacking in the Old City, a modern Beyoğlu–Galata day of meyhane mezes and fine dining, and a final day of Anatolian home cooking in Kadıköy on the Asian side. Paced with walks between meals and light arrival/departure days.
